title: Designing data structures

overview.what: The process of combining primitive data structures (like arrays, hash maps, and linked lists) into a composite structure to achieve specific time complexity goals for various operations.
overview.why: No single built-in data structure is perfectly fast at everything. To build a system that can quickly insert, delete, and fetch the minimum element, you must weave multiple structures together.
where_used: LRU Caches (Hash Map + Doubly Linked List)

why_learning_this: It tests your deep understanding of the tradeoffs of every primitive structure.
'Design X' is one of the most common formats for senior-level coding interviews.
It mirrors real-world object-oriented class design.

common_mistakes.title: Ignoring state synchronization
common_mistakes.explanation: When using two structures (e.g., a Hash Map and an Array), inserting or deleting an item must update BOTH structures. Forgetting to keep them perfectly in sync leads to dangling pointers or ghost data.

common_mistakes.title: Not starting from the constraints
common_mistakes.explanation: If a problem asks for O(1) retrieval, you almost certainly need a Hash Map. If it asks for O(1) removal of the oldest item, you need a Queue or Linked List. Not mapping constraints to primitives first is a planning failure.

recall_questions.q: If you need O(1) lookups and O(1) deletion from the middle of a sequence, what composite structure should you use?
recall_questions.answer: A Hash Map containing pointers to nodes of a Doubly Linked List.

recall_questions.q: Why is an array poor for O(1) arbitrary deletion, and how can a Hash Map help if order doesn't matter?
recall_questions.answer: Arrays require O(N) shifts to delete. If order doesn't matter, you can swap the element to delete with the last element and pop it in O(1). A Hash Map tracks the array indices of each element so you know what to swap.

understanding_checks.question: You need a data structure that supports `insert(val)`, `remove(val)`, and `getRandom()` all in O(1) average time. Which composition of structures should you use?
understanding_checks.answer: A Hash Map and an Array (Dynamic Array / List).
understanding_checks.why: `getRandom()` in O(1) requires an Array for contiguous indexing. `insert` and `remove` in O(1) require a Hash Map to find elements in the array to swap-and-pop.

understanding_checks.question: In an LRU Cache made of a Hash Map and Doubly Linked List, what happens to the Linked List when an existing key is accessed?
understanding_checks.answer: The node representing that key is unlinked from its current position and moved to the 'most recently used' end (usually the head or tail, depending on convention).
understanding_checks.why: Accessing an item refreshes its status, pushing it as far away from eviction as possible.
